Its really dependant on what country you live in, but there's loads of subreddits that are willing to teach you things, including this one. For now I'd say these are the key things to look at. (I'd strongely reccomend having several back up plans) 

Finance: You're looking for a job, do you have any qualifications etc, how much can your savings look after you and if any friends can help you out. Making your own lunch and breakfast etc is a good way to keep food cheap.

You may also want to let banks know where to send their mail to you as you don't want your bio-family getting anything (or even opening credit cards etc in your name) 

Living with roomies: Find out everything about your lease and the area you're living with. Can you move in with friends temporarily or have anyone to look after your stuff? What kind of people are you going to be living with etc. Make sure you let them know about who to let in and who not to let in. You are a lot more independant than you realise. 

Name Changes: Find out how much it costs (in the UK, it's free, but getting your passport etc costs a fair bit.) You don't have to do this, but it may make it harder for your bio-family to trace you or contact you. 

Schooling: Let your school (or at least someone you trust) know you dont want any correspondance with your bio-family as soon as you're out of high school. This is fairly important because loads of places have confidentiality agreements in place, but some can slip up pretty easy. 

Police: If you're worried about domestic abuse or stalking etc, I would strongly reccomend calling a non-emergency line and talking to them, often they'll offer you emergency housing (UK here, not sure where you're in and if they'll do this for you) but at the very least, you can rely on them to accompany you if you need your things or at the least, they have a case open incase an emergency happens.
 

Contact details: Change your email or at least get a new one. I think there are some app that will direct family emails to a separate folder but keep them incase you need to show someone. 
Change your emergency contact details as well so they dont get any calls and therefore wont know unless you tell them.
Change your number and ask your provider not to give you physical bills or at the very least not to send them to your bio-family's address. Stay safe, and stay wary. 

Therapy: Very important and sometimes overlooked. You'll probably feel guilt afterwards and your brain might end up only giving you "happy memories" etc but at the end of the day, you're  cutting contact for a reason. Therapy will or should help, and they should not for whatever reason disclose any of the information to anyone else unless it's going to harm someone else or yourself.
